Putin’s Bid to End the War in Ukraine on Moscow’s Terms
 
Plus, a little-known private trust is looming over Anthropic’s IPO, and French leaders are trading blame after rioting sweeps the nation
 
 
BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP/GETTY IMAGES
 

1. FROM MY DESK

 

Vladimir Putin has proposed that he, President Trump and Xi Jinping meet next month to talk about Ukraine and negotiate a favorable end to the war for Moscow.

 

The plan represents an attempt by Putin to capitalize on warming ties with Trump. But such a summit—one without Volodymyr Zelensky—would be unprecedented and send alarm bells ringing in Europe and beyond.

 

Putin floated the idea in an Oct. 9 phone call with Trump, a former Russian intelligence officer told the Journal. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that discussions were taking place over a potential meeting.

 

With the midterms just two weeks away, Trump’s overtures to Russia have become a headache for Republican candidates. Republicans are being pressed on why now is the time to go soft on Putin—and some are breaking with Trump rather than defending his string of Russia-friendly decisions.

 

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here. If you’re reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

• Some Wall Street leaders are weighing bailing on “Davos in the Desert” in Saudi Arabia next week after attacks on Riyadh. The country has advanced weaponry, but Yemen’s Houthis have proved to be a resilient foe.

 

• Trump administration officials are lawyering up, preparing for the possibility that Democrats could launch probes if the party takes back Congress.

 

• French leaders are trading blame after rioting has swept the nation.
